rules.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.5 (Security deposits)
rules.requirement: On transfer of a landlord's interest, the landlord must transfer the remaining deposit to the successor or return it to the tenant with an accounting. Successors are jointly liable for noncompliance. Leases may not call a deposit "nonrefundable", and bad faith retention can bring statutory damages.
rules.key_value: Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith retention
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages, for bad faith claim or retention of the deposit.
rules.status_basis: Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1 (AB 414). Effective January 1, 2026.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords of residential rental property holding security deposits.

rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”
